I read the whole file (lines 1–89) and judged it from the text alone. I did not open the imported files or search the source roots.

The only repeated reasoning is in `resK0_eq_basisEquiv` and `symmetricThreeStabilizerSimpleClassBasis_repr_resK0`. Both run `apply (symmetricThreeCharThreeSimpleClassBasis k).ext; intro b` and then use `resK0_stabilizer_perm_fin_three_simpleClassBasis_apply`. This is a routine "two linear maps agree on a basis" argument.

The mathematical content is already factored into the simp lemma `resK0_stabilizer_perm_fin_three_simpleClassBasis_apply`. What remains in each proof is a few lines of rewriting, and the two goals differ in shape. One goal is an equality of linear maps into `Module.Basis.equiv`; the other is a composition with `repr`.

A possible simplification is to derive bijectivity from the `repr` lemma. That lemma says `resK0 = (stabilizer basis).repr.symm ∘ (S₃ basis).repr`, so `resK0` is bijective as a composite of equivalences. This would remove the private lemma `resK0_eq_basisEquiv`. The saving is a handful of lines and the lemma is private. I judged this too small to meet the rubric's threshold of nontrivial repeated machinery, so I report no finding.
